method: Same number densities, temperature, speed, geometry, attitude, kernel and accommodation; only the species mass table differs. No atmosphere model is called and no propagation is run.
question: Holding the state fixed, what force difference does this project's integer-mass-number convention produce against NRLMSIS 2.1's own CIPM 2007 masses?
what_this_does_not_establish: Any end-to-end propagation bias. A trajectory integrates the force over a changing state and a systematic force offset does not map linearly onto a threshold-crossing time. No crossing-time claim is made from this.
why_they_differ: If drag were simply linear in density at fixed everything else, these two relative differences would be equal and their ratio exactly 1. They are not, because s_j is proportional to sqrt(m_j), so changing the masses also moves every speed ratio and hence every per-species coefficient. The ratio reported above is the measured size of that departure.
